item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 242322
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Oct 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located a few hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms are a little better organized in
association with a broad area of low pressure located just west of
the International Date Line, several hundred miles west of Johnston
Atoll. Some development of this system is possible over the next few
days while it moves east-northeastward at 10 to 15 mph. By the
middle of next week, however, strong upper-level winds should limit
any additional development.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.description: ...VANCE HOLDS STEADY WHILE DRIFTING NORTH-NORTHWESTWARD... As of 9:00 PM CST Sat Oct 24 the center of Vance was located near 13.7, -103.4 with movement NNW at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 977 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 90 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Vance Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 250244
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Vance Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026
 
...VANCE HOLDS STEADY WHILE DRIFTING NORTH-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.7N 103.4W
ABOUT 320 MI...515 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 370 MI...595 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance. 
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Vance was located
near latitude 13.7 North, longitude 103.4 West. Vance is moving
slowly toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue through Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Fluctuations in strength are likely through Monday, followed 
by steady weakening after that. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through next Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 4 to 6
inches with isolated higher totals around 10 inches across Colima
and western portions of Michoacán and Jalisco. This rainfall may
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of 
southern and southwestern Mexico into next week. These swells are 
likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. 
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Vance Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 250245
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Vance Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Sat Oct 24 2026
 
Vance continues to look disorganized on satellite images, and it 
seems that southwesterly shear is keeping the convection displaced 
from the center. The hurricane is also moving over cool waters, 
which is also inhibiting intensification as well. GPM microwave 
images show that the structure of the cyclone is vertically tilted 
due to the aforementioned shear. Despite the system's ragged 
appearance, the Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB is still 
T5.0/90 kt while the objective intensity estimates are in the range 
of 68-81 kt. Therefore, the initial intensity has been kept to 80 kt 
based on a combination of that data, however, it could be generous. 
 
The intensity forecast still has plenty of uncertainties. Vance is 
generally expected to weaken during the next 12 h due to the 
continuous of shear while it remains over cool SSTs. After that 
time, the hurricane's intensity could fluctuate when Vance moves 
over warmer waters, but the wind shear will likely remain elevated. 
After 48 h, the wind shear is expected to increase even further and 
that should result in a gradual weakening trend. It is possible 
that Vance could weaken more than forecast given the expected 
increasing shear and intrusions of dry air. The NHC intensity 
forecast is generally similar to the previous one with only a few 
minor adjustments made. 
 
The initial motion remains slowly north-northwestward or 340/4 kt. 
The cyclone is currently being steered by a weak low- to mid-level 
ridge over eastern Mexico, and it is moving toward a large 
mid-latitude trough over the western United States and northwestern 
Mexico. Vance should move into an area where the steering currents 
are light, thus the hurricane is expected to move even slower over 
the next few days. The latest guidance shifted significantly to the 
west compared to the previous forecast, including the highly skilled 
forecast aids HCCA and GDMI, which has added some uncertainty in the 
track forecast. The new track forecast was adjusted slightly to the 
west and is a little slower than the previous one. However, the 
current track is on the eastern side of the guidance envelope, and 
additional adjustments to the west could be needed. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Due to the uncertainties in both the track and intensity
forecasts, it is too early to say what wind and storm surge
impacts Vance may cause along the coast of Mexico. Interests in
southwestern Mexico should continue to monitor the progress of the
hurricane.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with slow-moving Hurricane Vance will
impact the western coast of Mexico from Michoacán to Jalisco during
much of next week. This rainfall may produce life-threatening
flooding and mudslides across Colima and western portions of
Michoacán and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
